newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan Life's loss bigger than its estimate - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nissan Life's loss bigger than its estimate - paper.

text.p: Unrealised losses on assets held at Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co far exceed the firm's estimate, a Japanese business daily said on Thursday.

Last month, Nissan Life said that it expects to report a parent net loss of 52.5 billion yen for the business year ended March 31 and unrealised losses of 132.8 billion yen on assets such as securities and real estate holdings.

But the Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported that an inspection by the Life Insurance Association of Japan had found that the unrealised losses were much higher than the firm's estimate, and had put the figure at 250 billion yen.
A spokesman at the life insurers' body said that the association had not yet completed its inspection of Nissan Life's assets, so could not give a figure.
"The inspection is expected to continue at least until the end of this month," he said.
The association is charged with the task of overseeing what remains of Nissan Life's operations after the firm collapsed last month under the weight of accumulated losses.
Industry sources said that the Policyholders Protection Fund, established in 1996, will provide 200 billion yen to protect Nissan Life policyholders.
The association has been working out various options for cleaning up the mess, including liquidating Nissan Life's operations or transferring them to a new company.
